data.title: Carlos Slim Helu Discloses 6.5% Stake in BRASKEM SA
data.description:
Carlos Slim Helu Discloses 6.5% Stake in BRASKEM SA

Carlos Slim Helu and related reporting persons disclosed beneficial ownership of a 6.5% stake in BRASKEM SA’s Class A preferred shares, held through American depositary shares. They filed the Schedule 13D on November 6, 2026, using the company’s June 30 share count to calculate their combined stake. The group says it bought the shares for investment, not to change or influence control of BRASKEM SA.

Investor Intent

The group says it has no current plan to change BRASKEM SA’s business or control. It will review its investment and could discuss the company with management, directors or other shareholders, or propose changes to its capitalization, board or operations. The group also says it may buy or sell shares in the future.

Investor's Background

Carlos Slim Helu is a Mexican businessman and the lead individual in a group that includes members of his family, Control Empresarial and two Mexican foundations. A Mexican trust that benefits the Slim family owns all of Control Empresarial’s voting securities. The filing says boards with Slim family members in the majority make investment decisions for Fundacion Carlos Slim and Fundacion Telmex.

Original SEC Filing: BRASKEM SA [ BAK ] - SCHEDULE 13D - Nov. 06, 2026

data.title: Brent crude caps biggest weekly drop since pandemic as war premium begins to unwind
data.description:
Crude oil futures finished little changed Friday but Brent crude ended with its largest weekly loss since the COVID-19 pandemic, after heavy losses suffered by Republicans in the U.S. midterm elections raised expectations that the Trump administration will pursue a diplomatic solution to the conflict with Iran.

This week saw "the reversal of the substantial risk premium that had accrued across September and October despite resilient Middle East flows and rapidly normalizing global oil balances," Macquarie energy strategist Walt Chancellor said in a note.

Previous worries over a potential escalation in the Middle East have "given way to a renewed diplomatic push, less hawkish rhetoric from Trump, and apparent Republican introspection about the war in the aftermath of the midterms," Chancellor wrote.

Bloomberg reported Friday that the U.S. and Iran have moved closer to a potential breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Iran showing a willingness to discuss issues related to its nuclear program that were previously off the table.

Iran is studying proposals related to its atomic activities that were presented by chief mediator Qatar, and President Trump recently spoke by phone with Qatar's leader about efforts to de-escalate tensions, according to the report.

Physical oil prices are also signaling an easing in global supply conditions, and analysts at J.P. Morgan said this week that the global oil market is moving back into surplus as Middle Eastern exports recover and demand weakens.

Global supply exceeded demand by 1.1M bbl/day in September and widened to 1.4M bbl/day in October, while Middle Eastern oil exports recovered to 20.7M bbl/day in October from a low of 9.8M bbl/day in March during the first month of the war, the bank estimated.

Global oil demand has declined by 3.3M bbl/day since the conflict began, JPM also said, reflecting the impact of higher fuel prices and supply disruptions.

Nevertheless, the recovery in oil flows from the Middle East remains at risk due to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea export route.

A Greek ship manager said a seafarer was killed in a November 5 explosion on an oil products tanker in the Persian Gulf, believed to have been caused by a missile attack.

Data from U.K. maritime security agency UKMTO suggested that attacks on oil-carrying ships are still running at close to a record pace.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude for December delivery edged up 0.3% to $90.83/bbl and front-month Brent crude for December delivery gained $0.03 to $98.32/bbl.

For the full week, U.S. crude plunged 12.7%, its biggest one week percentage decline since the week ending April 17, and Brent crude sank 13.3%, its largest one week percentage loss since the week ending April 24, 2020.

U.S. natural gas futures gained as some cooler weather entered into the latest weather forecasts, lifting the front-month Nymex contract for December delivery up 1.7% to $2.998/MMBtu, its best settlement value since October 19; for the week, U.S. natgas gained 3.4%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF , tumbled 12% this week.

(FSE: 8BS) ("GPI" or the "Company") announces that it has engaged MCS Market Communication Services GmbH ("MCS") (address: Saarlandstraße 28, 58511 Lüdenscheid, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany; info@mcsmarket.de; +49 177 248 1220), for marketing services for an expected term of six month, commencing immediately. The term of the marketing services may be extended or shortened at the discretion of management depending on, amongst other things, the efficacy of the marketing services.

Pursuant to the engagement, MCS will provide a comprehensive suite of digital marketing services including, among other things: the development and management of digital campaigns, the creation of text materials; detailed keyword research and campaign optimization; creation of customized landing pages and coordination with online marketers; and placements across various online channels to improve reach and visibility. MCS will execute these services through online platforms using demographic, geographic, keyword, and interest-based targeting to reach relevant investor audiences.

The Company will pay a total fee of €500,000 (inclusive of advertising spend and an 18% agency fee) for the term, with the total fee being split into three payments throughout the term, with the first payment of €166,666 being paid immediately. MCS does not currently hold any securities of the Company and no securities-based compensation has been provided or is contemplated in connection with the engagement. MCS is a third-party marketing services provider and is at arm's length to the Company.

About Good Purpose Investments

Good Purpose Investments Inc. is a sustainability-focused company that acquires, develops, and scales environmentally aligned businesses operating across circular materials, sustainable manufacturing technologies, and next-generation consumer product categories. The Company aims to build a diversified portfolio of investments and internally developed businesses supported by shared infrastructure, commercial expertise, and centralized innovation capabilities. Its initial portfolio company is Waste2Wear, a wholly owned subsidiary of GPI and provider of circular textile and product solutions.
